summary: Name the feature “Canvas Templates.” The owning capability is `canvases`, because the behavior snapshots and applies canvas layout state. It is not owned by `organizations` or `billing`; “workspace” is reserved for tenant organizations, while the editor term becomes “canvas template.” Authorization follows the destination canvas project membership.

tree.purpose: Server-only persistence with destination-canvas/project ownership predicates.
Checks source access when saving and destination project membership when applying.
Authenticated Server Component read surface for listing templates available to a destination canvas.
Top-level Server Actions for save and apply mutations; validates untrusted form/input data and returns serializable action state.
Explicit reusable editor UI surface for template picker/save controls.
Route composition only; renders the editor and consumes the canvases surfaces.

flows: Read: `app/(editor)/projects/[projectId]/canvases/[canvasId]/page.tsx` → `src/modules/canvases/rsc.ts` → authenticate actor → `template-store.ts.listForDestination(canvasId, actor)` → enforce destination project membership → return renderable template summaries. Server Components should read capability data directly rather than call an internal Route Handler. [Next.js Server and Client Components](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components)

Save: editor UI → `src/modules/canvases/actions.ts.saveCanvasTemplate(formData)` → authenticate actor → validate source canvas ID, name, and layout snapshot → `template-policy.ts` verifies source-canvas access → `template-store.ts` persists the snapshot → return serializable action state and invalidate the editor’s relevant cache.

Apply: editor UI → `src/modules/canvases/actions.ts.applyCanvasTemplate(formData)` → authenticate actor → validate template ID and destination canvas ID → `template-policy.ts` verifies destination project membership → `template-store.ts` atomically loads the template and updates the destination canvas layout → return serializable action state and invalidate destination-canvas data. Server Actions are appropriate for these UI mutations and are reachable through POST, so authorization must occur inside the action and again at the capability/store boundary. [Next.js Mutating Data](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data)

decisions.rationale: Separates reusable editor layouts from tenant organizations, which retain the product term “workspace” in authentication and billing.
The feature changes canvas layout state and its critical authorization edge is membership of the destination canvas’s project.

decisions.choice: No new organizations or billing dependency
decisions.rationale: The feature neither provisions organizations nor changes subscriptions or tenant lifecycle. Project membership is consumed through the existing canvases/project authorization boundary.

decisions.choice: `rsc.ts` for reads and `actions.ts` for editor mutations; no Route Handler
decisions.rationale: The named consumers are the editor Server Component and browser UI. Route Handlers are unnecessary without an external HTTP or browser-GET contract.

decisions.choice: Authenticate at each public channel, validate inputs there, enforce membership in policy and store predicates
decisions.rationale: Client fields and hidden IDs are not authoritative; defense in depth prevents applying a template to an unauthorized destination.

risks: The task does not define whether templates are reusable across tenants or projects; the proposal assumes the template record is capability-owned and that applying it is authorized by the destination project membership as specified.
If templates later gain sharing, publishing, versioning, or cross-project ownership rules, extract those policies into an explicit `canvas-templates` capability rather than overloading `canvases`.
